web-snapper.name: Web Snapper
web-snapper.tagline: Turn any web page into a searchable, annotatable, archivable asset.
web-snapper.seoTitle: Web Snapper - Full-page screenshots, searchable PDF & web archiving
web-snapper.seoDescription: Capture full web pages or regions, export searchable PDFs and single-file HTML, redact and annotate, extract Markdown, and archive everything to a private local history - all on your device.
web-snapper.description: A privacy-first capture workbench for the web. Take full-page or region screenshots and export them as searchable PDF, PNG, single-file HTML, or clean Markdown; extract just the core article; redact and annotate the page in one editor; and archive every capture to a searchable local history - all in a local sandbox.

highlights.title: Searchable PDF export
highlights.desc: Exported PDFs carry an invisible text layer: copy text, run a full-text search, and click the original links - in any language, with almost no extra file size.

highlights.title: Full-page & region capture
highlights.desc: Smart scroll-stitching captures long pages and fixes sticky-header ghosting, or drag-select any region you want.

highlights.title: Lossless single-file HTML
highlights.desc: Save a whole page as one HTML file with images, styles, and fonts inlined. It opens offline, with scripts and trackers stripped.

highlights.title: Edit the page, then save
highlights.desc: A built-in page editor: black out, mosaic, or truly delete any element or text - nothing sensitive is left - then add highlights, notes, and tags before you export the cleaned-up page.

highlights.title: Reader mode & Markdown
highlights.desc: Extract just the core article - automatically dropping sidebars, headers, footers, and ads - then export clean, semantic Markdown for Obsidian, Typora, or VS Code.

highlights.title: Searchable local archive
highlights.desc: Every capture is auto-saved to a local history with thumbnails, full-text search, and SHA-256 hashes - zero cloud, instant response.

privacyPoints: Capture, packaging, screenshots, and redaction all run in a local sandbox
Redaction truly removes content - no sensitive data remains in the exported file
Built on Chrome Manifest V3 with minimal, activeTab-based permissions
Non-AI features never go online; history and annotations stay on your device
steps: Open any page and capture the full page or a selected region
Redact anything sensitive, then highlight and annotate what matters
Export to searchable PDF, HTML, or Markdown - auto-archived to local history

deepDive.title: Professional capture
deepDive.desc: Smart scrolling stitches long pages - handling sticky headers and sidebars - or drag-select a region. Export to PNG, searchable PDF, or Markdown on fit-to-content, A4, or Letter.

deepDive.title: Lossless HTML archive
deepDive.desc: Save a whole page as a single HTML file with images, styles, and fonts inlined. It opens offline as a clean, static snapshot with scripts and trackers removed.

deepDive.title: Edit the page, then save
deepDive.desc: Edit the page before you save: black out, mosaic, or delete any element or text - truly removed, with nothing left in the export - then add highlights, notes, and tags. Highlights even export as real, editable PDF annotations, and everything restores on revisit.

deepDive.title: Reader mode & Markdown
deepDive.desc: Extract just the core article, automatically dropping sidebars, headers, footers, and ads. Export clean, semantic Markdown - real text, original image references, and true-color highlights - for Obsidian, Typora, or VS Code.

faq.question: Are the exported PDFs searchable?
faq.answer: Yes. PDF exports include an invisible text layer, so you can select and copy text, run a full-text search, and click the original links - in any language, with almost no increase in file size.

faq.question: Does redaction really remove the content?
faq.answer: Yes. Redaction deletes the underlying element or text rather than just covering it, so no sensitive information remains in the exported file.

faq.question: Can I open a saved page offline?
faq.answer: Yes. The single-file HTML packs images, styles, and fonts inline and strips scripts and trackers, so it opens anywhere as a clean, static snapshot.

faq.question: Does Web Snapper upload my pages?
faq.answer: No. Capture, packaging, and redaction run in a local sandbox, and your history and annotations are stored on your device. Non-AI features never touch the network.

faq.question: Where do my captures go?
faq.answer: Every capture is archived to a searchable local history with thumbnails and SHA-256 hashes. You can reopen the original page, locate the file, or delete it - all local, no cloud.

About.title: About browserextensions.co
About.subtitle: A small studio building focused browser extensions that do one thing well - and keep your data on your device.

mission.title: What we're about
mission.body: browserextensions.co builds a growing suite of browser extensions for everyday work: capturing pages, exporting AI conversations, and making sense of reviews. Each one is designed to be fast, focused, and free of the bloat that makes most extensions a chore. We'd rather ship a few tools people genuinely rely on than a long list nobody trusts.

products.title: What we build
products.body: Our current tools are Web Snapper for capturing and saving web pages, AI Chat Snapper for exporting conversations from ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and seven other AI assistants, and Review Snapper for summarizing product reviews. They share a common philosophy: a clear job, a clean interface, and no surprises.

privacy.title: Privacy by default
privacy.body: We build local-first. Wherever it's possible, our extensions do their work directly on your device, without accounts and without uploading your content to a server. AI Chat Snapper, for example, generates exports entirely in your browser and can run fully offline. Your data is yours - we'd rather not handle it at all.

contact.title: Get in touch
contact.body: We read everything. Share feedback, request a feature, or report a bug through our feedback page, or email us directly at support@browserextensions.co.
